newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan body to boost penalties to prevent scandals.
newsitem.headline: Japan body to boost penalties to prevent scandals.

text.p: The Japan Securities Dealers Association (JSDA) said on Wednesday it had decided to strengthen its penalties for financial wrongdoing to prevent future scandals.

Tsugio Yukihira, chairman of the self-regulatory body for Japan's brokerages, told a news conference that penalties would be reinforced but did not say by how much. The current penalty is a fine of 100 million yen for financial wrongdoing, he said.
Besides boosting financial penalties, the body will also adopt such measures as checking internal management control and strengthening the JSDA's investigation system.
He said the JSDA would wait for the finance ministry's punishment on Nomura Securities Co Ltd which is expected later this month and will punish Nomura in line with the ministry's penalties.
He said the schedule for the new measures had not been decided, but added that they are expected by the end of this year.
